utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case and bring the accused in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The usual routine, Mr. Brdjanin. I would like you to confirm to me that you are hearing me in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I can hear you and I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And General Talic, good morning to you too. Are you in a position to make the same affirmation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I can hear you and I do understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And while we are at it, may I remind you of what I told you yesterday, and I would like you to confirm again what you confirmed to me yesterday since your counsel, Mr. de Roux and Mr. Pitron, are not present today as well, whether we have your consent to go ahead as you actually promised yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree that we can continue the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So appearances. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours, my name is Cayley. I appear with Ms. Korner on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope you don't take this as a need that the Presidency of the Trial Chamber has to refresh its memory as to who is appearing in the Chamber. In fact, if you agree, we might as well do without this, but I was told there was a custom here that they resort to this, but frankly, once we have a trial that we've started and which will go on for God knows how long, we could as well forget all about it. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just remarked to Mr. Cayley that I've never understood why each day we have to announce who we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the only purpose of this exercise is so that the record shows who was actually in Court representing the accused on that particular day, and I believe we have court reporters that are smart enough to figure that out and can put that in the record just as a routine thing every morning. In any event, at least today it's John Ackerman for Mr. Brdjanin, along with Ms. Tania Radosavljevic, Milka Maglov, and Milos Peric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Natasha Fauveau-Ivanovic, a lawyer from the Paris bar, and I am replacing Mr. Pitron and Mr. de Roux, and I am assisted by Mr. Fabien Masson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So are there any things or matters that you would like to bring up, raise before we start, continue with the cross-examination of Dr. Donia?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, only to say that the list will be available, I hope by the break, where all the documents come from, which can then be given to counsel for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's perfect, Ms. Korner. So please bring in the witness, Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where is he?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I did see him, Your Honour, this morning. I wasn't speaking to him because he is now under cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was beginning to worry he went back to the States. Here he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may sit down. Mr. Ackerman will resume -- continue with his cross-examination. Please go ahead, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Donia. How are you this morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good. Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I guess I would be remiss, having looked at all of the other cross-examinations that people have done of you, if I didn't say you've got a foundation called the Donia Vakuf Foundation, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Where did you come up with the name "Donia Vakuf"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The name came from the municipality of Donja Vakuf, which is very close to my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And because your name is Donia, Donia Vakuf just flowed together for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: At the time you did that, were you aware of the meaning of the word "Vakuf"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber what that word means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Vakuf" is a Serbo-Croatian word that is a derivative of the Arabic "wakif," which means a charitable foundation established typically by wealthy Muslim family to endow a particular religious, cultural, or educational institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Would you say that it most often has a religious connotation to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A blend often of the three, really. Since most educational institutions are religious in nature, I would say yes, it most often does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. I want to look at Prosecution Exhibit Number 13, which is at Tab 10 of Book 1 and ask you to go to page 13 of that document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, may I ask the tab number again? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And page?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 13. The speaker is Dr. Karadzic, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In that first full paragraph following the round of applause, about two-thirds of the way down, Dr. Karadzic, in speaking of the Serb nation, says, does he not, that, "It is a nation well known for its tendency towards disunity and discord due to its strong individualistic nature"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If you look at the reports of all of these assembly sessions that we have in here, that tends to be -- that statement tends to be proven by the nature of some of the arguments that we see going on in the sessions, that these people are not agreeing with each other all the time and there is quite a bit of discord and disunity going on among them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, these sessions certainly support that view, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you see the disputes that were going on between what I was calling yesterday the Pale group and the Banja Luka group or, as you corrected me, the Sarajevo group and the Banja Luka group. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, this particular document that we're looking at right now is the session of 12 July 1991. On 12 July 1991, it is still the position, is it not, of Karadzic and his followers that Bosnia-Herzegovina should remain a part of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And this meeting was mostly -- I would say mostly characterised by disagreements over the issue of regionalisation and what form that was to take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And on page 25 of that meeting, I think -- yes, it's page 25, Dr. Karadzic speaking again. About halfway down you'll find a sentence that I think that reads as follows: "I have to say one thing. We have to preserve the strength of the party not to give in to power-grabbing impulses and the little Napoleons who are trying to do things that will harm the Serbian people." I take it that you would agree that he was talking about that Banja Luka group and perhaps Mr. Brdjanin in particular when he talked about "little Napoleons"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's at this point, is it not, that Dr. Karadzic starts to talk about his concept of what -- how regionalisation is to work.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He says, does he not, there, as we get down to, like, the last quarter of page 25: "I assure you, municipal boards do not want to have any umbrella over them except for the main board. Regional boards are thus a place where the work of all municipal boards in a region is coordinated and not a power above the municipal boards. To be more specific and to take an example, it was said at the time in Bosnian Krajina, Bosanski Novi ..." which is municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "... Bosanski Novi said, `All right, we will do it, but don't think that we will allow Banja Luka to be to Bosanski Novi what Sarajevo is to Banja Luka.' It would not be democratic. Quite the contrary; it would be anti-democratic -- it would be an anti-democratic ..." And then the next page: "... framework in which we would make it impossible for individual municipalities to work directly with the main board." Continuing: "I think it is sufficient for the regional board to be composed of all the presidents of municipal boards and for them to coordinate their work there. In that way, it is impossible to force any municipal organisation or municipal board to do anything. It is the only way." If you go to the next page. About a third of the way down of page 27: "It is better to have the entire municipal board making decisions than for it to become alienated. Power corrupts, gentlemen." The next paragraph: "Just as regional boards, which would be a power structure above municipal boards instead of coordinating bodies, would be a source of great trouble and would cause a great deal of screaming and wailing in the municipal boards." Near the bottom last full paragraph: "Thus we from the main board are not a power above the municipal boards either except for the fact that we ask them to implement party policies." Now, those were all of the -- or many of the things that Dr. Karadzic said about this, the concept of regionalisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If we go then to page 28. In that first paragraph you find the language: "That is why we have decided regional boards, yes. They are coordinating bodies made up of the presidents of the municipal boards, and no one has power over others. But we have to be on our guard lest we should institutionalise it, impose it, and create conditions for power grabbing." Now, one thing that Dr. Karadzic is saying there is just sort of an obvious concession to the reality of the situation that the municipal boards tended to be the main source of power and very jealous of all their prerogatives. And as -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I just -- he is speaking here at a party meeting of party boards. I think that's perhaps clear, but just to make that distinction. He makes occasional references to municipal assemblies, but he's speaking principally of municipal boards of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But municipal assemblies are basically the same sort of organisations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they're not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, let me -- let me put that in a different way. The boards of the municipalities are elected representatives from the people that live in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The municipal board of the party, the SDS, I wouldn't characterise it that way, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm talking about a municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A municipal assembly consists of those deputies -- at this time, those deputies who were elected in the multi-party election of November 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And when you're talking about the situation that developed in the ARK region with the establishment of Serbian municipalities, in many cases you're talking about the same people serving on the -- in the municipal assemblies as were serving on the municipal boards of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This -- these remarks are made at a time well in advance of the creation of Serbian assemblies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There's no question about that. But what Dr. Karadzic is talking about is the nature of the Serbian people and with regard to their -- of the power politics that go on between and among them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I agree there is a tendency to, say, refer to the SDS and government in kind of overlapping terms, but his comments here which are in the context of the discussion of the statute of the SDS pertain to the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. That's not the point I'm trying to make with you. The point I'm trying to make with you is this: The Serb people, the Serb representatives who made up the municipal assemblies, were primarily SDS, certainly Serbs, and certainly part of this contentious people that he talks about here, the same people; not necessarily the same names, but the same people. And what he says about the jealousies of power and how those people in the municipalities are reluctant to be told by anyone else what to do, that they feel like they are a power in themselves, tends to be the way those people felt; when they were elected in municipalities, that they were the power in that municipality and certainly didn't want anybody except perhaps the Republican government making policy for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object at this point. This is not a question. This is a speech. Dr. Donia has already made the point this speech by Dr. Karadzic was made in July of 1991. That is well before the Serbian assemblies were even formed. And here, Mr. Ackerman is testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are perfectly right that it is a statement more than a question, and a long one at that. So without asking for a reply from you, I would like you to rephrase your statement into a question and put it direct to the witness, because the objection raised is very much a valid one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think I'll just go forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Would you look, please, at page 29.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Right at the bottom, Dr. Karadzic says: "A part of our main board broke away and created something they called the homeland front, not Kupresanin's front but some other homeland front, which is doing stupid things, beating its head against a brick, pushing forward without any political logic, and causing great political damage to the Serbian people." Do you know what he's talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Would you go to page 90 of this document. I think maybe you have to go back two pages before those lists of people, but it's true, is it not, that what they are doing at this point is they are voting for members of the main board from the various areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina and actually electing members of the main board?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, the main board of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah. And I'm drawing your attention to page 90, which involves the vote for persons from the Bosnian Krajina, and it lists in order the candidates from the Bosnian Krajina and the number of votes that each one of them received, and then lists the eight who were the highest vote-getters as having been elected to the main board. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on page 91 -- right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. In the list of candidates and the list of those elected, Mr. Brdjanin's name does not appear at all, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Excuse me, it does not appear as a contestant either.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does not appear either as a contestant, as a candidate, nor as being elected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Under Tab 1, you will find Prosecution Exhibit 16. And the place I want to refer you in that document is to -- first of all, this document is a document from the ZOBK. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the Presidency of the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Dated 6th September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And signed by Vojo Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of that, he says, "Having examined the data and reports from the war-affected area, the Presidency decided that the facts reveal a considerable concentration of the Republic of Croatia armed forces in the territory of Okucani and Stari Gradiska and their activities against the Serb civilian population. What is it he's referring to there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Look at the next document, which is Prosecution Exhibit 17 under Tab 14.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Under paragraph -- first of all, what's happening there is this is a decision, if you go back to page 29, on the verification of the proclaimed Serbian autonomous regions in Bosnia and Herzegovina, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And the first two lines, it indicates that one of those regions that's being verified is the ARK.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Go then to the next page, paragraph 3: "The rights and obligations of the Serbian autonomous districts, the manner in which these rights and obligations are exercised, organisation of bodies, and other matters significant for the exercise of rights and obligations of the Serbian autonomous districts shall be regulated by separate decision." Can you point us to that separate decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The decision I would assume this is looking forward to would be the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I know of no other separate decision that was undertaken by the assembly of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Wouldn't you think if it was talking about the constitution, it would say "matters significant for the exercise of rights and obligations of the Serbian autonomous districts shall be regulated by the constitution"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. In the flow of events, this -- your first document, I believe, was to 6 September 1991. This meeting is on 21 November 1991, so some, what, two and-a-half months later. By this time, the decision to form a Serbian republic was under consideration but had not been declared; and furthermore, the notion of a constitution would have at this point been considered a provocation to the other groups and international negotiators just as it was in February 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could you go to Prosecution's Exhibit 17B - that's the B/C/S version of this document - and find that same paragraph in B/C/S for me and tell me what page it's on. I think you'll find it on page 32.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is on page 32 as I see the reference. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's paragraph three and page 32, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 30 -- yes. 31 and 32 are reversed, in the reverse order here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: They are in mine, too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The word that is -- the word in Serbo-Croatian that's used in paragraph 3 that is translated as "decision" is the word "odlukom," which is commonly translated as "decision," is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I mean, it's not possible or realistic to translate that word as "constitution," is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. This -- this document and a number of the documents that we've been looking at for the last several days, Dr. Donia, are transcripts of the meetings of various boards, assemblies, organisations, things of that nature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And much of what we've been looking at are speeches made by various delegates or members of these various deliberative bodies; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you and I have both read portions of those speeches here in open court to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In terms of -- of what is -- what is actually established as law or policy, it's not, however, the speeches made by the politicians but the -- the laws and policies that are adopted after those speeches have been made that are really important for our purposes; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: For instance, the context in which you and I would probably best understand it is the United States Congress. We hear speeches on the floor of the United States Congress that go in all kinds of directions, and it would be a mistake to consider them as statements of the United States policy many times, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The difference is these people are in attendance, I think, in the Serbian assemblies, and in the United States Congress, often they're not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. When you say "not in attendance," you mean that speeches are made on the floor of the United States Senate by one senator all by himself? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And items are entered into the record without the representative even being present.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, that's true. You're talking about the Congressional Record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I wonder if the Trial Chamber has any idea what you and I are talking about now. And I'm not sure it matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would like you to proceed with further questioning -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Look at -- just for an example, if we look at tab 21, page 24 -- actually, it's page 13, I think. A person named Nenad Veselinovic is speaking, and he says in the second full paragraph that he has an idea about what should be done, that they should kind of break up municipalities and bring two or three of them together that contain Serb villages and create new Serb -- he's got a whole new idea about how to put this whole thing together is what he's saying in that paragraph, and of course that wasn't ever adopted as policy, it was just this one man's idea; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was done in a number of instances within Bosnia-Herzegovina at SDS initiative. This form of regionalisation was practised at the municipal level in ARK municipalities and elsewhere. As I indicated in this session when I talked about it, there is a resolution that is passed here subsequent to this involved discussion about regionalisation, and that document or that resolution endorses, that is, recommends the formation of Serbian municipalities. So this debate, I think, kind of, as is often the case in deliberative bodies such as this, illuminates the intent and the thinking of the delegates about the resolution and the reason it was passed as it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, if you look at that paragraph that I referred you to, maybe you don't agree with my interpretation of what it says, but I think what it says is -- what he is saying is where you have a Serb municipality and next to it is a municipality which is not Serb but has villages that are Serb, that you just go bring those villages into that other municipality, thereby increasing the size of the Serb municipality and diminishing the size of the non-Serb municipality and therefore creating basically a new municipality with a larger geographic area. If you go then to page 28 and look at the bottom of the page, there is a decision and it reads as follows: "The assembly unanimously, with the two mentioned supplements, adopted the proposed recommendation on the establishment of municipal assemblies of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the chairman so noted, adding that the cover letter would specify that this is recommended where necessary and should in no case be across the board because the latter would be unnecessary." Now, how does this square with the 11 December 1991 Variant A and B document? This seems to be saying, "Form the Serbian municipalities on a voluntary basis if you think it's necessary."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that document was 19 December. This is the 11 December assembly of the Serbian people meeting in which the topic of regionalisation is very broadly discussed. A recommendation was brought forward by Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik to form Serbian municipalities. It ran into substantial opposition from a number of deputies, and also some questions of what constituted regionalisation. And if you look at Rajko Dukic's address at this meeting, you will see that he has a similar understanding of regionalisation as Mr. Veselinovic did. But in this very broad discussion, what comes out is a recommendation. It is at this point constituted as a voluntary process for municipal boards to form Serbian assemblies. That voluntary dimension moves into this phase of a mandatory directive with the documentation of 19 December.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, that raises all kinds of interesting questions, because on the 11th of December, you've got the assembly of the Serbian people saying unanimously that the creation of Serbian assemblies is a voluntary thing and recommending it. Eight days later, in seeming violation of a unanimous decision of the assembly, you've got what is characterised as the SDS Crisis Staff issuing this Variant A, which you say is an order. How could they do that in the face of an assembly decision eight days earlier absolutely to the contrary? It would seem that the assembly is a higher power than the SDS Crisis Staff, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think the SDS assumed its complete control of the assembly and took the course of issuing these instructions on the 19th of December. This was then followed by the declaration of dozens of Serbian municipalities in Bosnia, some of them created immediately; some of them created well into February. And in February, we see, at the session of the 24th of February -- and many things have transpired in the meantime. But at the 24th of February, at that session, this has now reached the point where the leadership of the SDS at the Bosnian Serb assembly session says in a resolution, "This must be done in three days." There is a process here that moves forward from being a voluntary act by local boards to being required by the SDS main board or crisis staff, whichever, and finally being required by the Bosnian Serb assembly with a deadline provided, the same progressive steps that were followed in the affiliation of municipalities with the ARK. Over time, these approaches changed, became more mandatory, and were actually enforced by the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So it appears, then, that where we have gotten to with regard to this, Doctor, is that on 11 December, the assembly unanimously adopts this resolution regarding the voluntary establishment of Serbian municipalities. Eight days later, the Variant A/B document comes out which is obviously interpreted by virtually everyone in the municipalities as being a document that is simply implementing the decision of 11 December, that means being a voluntary document. And then I think what you're saying is that at some later point, there was then a new decision that "No, this document isn't really voluntary. We're going to order you to do this."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. As long as we're talking about the document under Tab 22, let me refer to it just for a moment. It's Prosecution Exhibit 25. It's your understanding, is it not, that this document -- you believe that this document was circulated by the main board to all of the -- all of the SDS municipal boards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There's nowhere in this document where any regional board or any regional organisation, ZOBK or ARK, is instructed to do anything. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Nowhere in this document is any responsibility assigned to any regional organisation for its implementation? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We're going to go now to the next volume, and the first document in that volume is Prosecution Exhibit 33. This exhibit is another meeting of the assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And this is what became Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the body that became the assembly of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Look at page 43. Again, in a speech by Karadzic -- and it's important that we understand this is a speech being made in the assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina; not in an SDS meeting, not in a regional meeting, but in the assembly itself. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic says at the very bottom of page 43, "This assembly is the supreme power of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina." This assembly, not the main board, not Karadzic, no one else, you are the supreme power. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So any regional organisation that acquires any power of any form must acquire it as a derivative power from this assembly of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is an assertion of Dr. Karadzic. I don't believe it became resolution. The constitution was adopted three days later, and I would assume that the relationship between this body and any regional entities would be defined in that constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, this was made in the presence of all of the delegates of the assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I assume they agreed with Mr. Karadzic, or they would have done something differently. And as a matter of fact, practically that's the way it was. That assembly was a supreme power, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not certain it was in all cases, no. I just would return to your point that this is a statement in the course of an assembly debate, not a resolution that was passed by this assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, if Dr. Karadzic viewed the assembly as the source of power and if all of the members of the assembly viewed the assembly as the source of power, then as a practical matter it was the source of power. Where I'm trying to go, and let me get there, in the way the Serbian people organised themselves into what became Republika Srpska, the power was in the government, which was in either Sarajevo or Pale, depending upon what period of time we're talking about. And no regional organisation, regional board, municipal organisation, or municipal board could define its own competence. Its competence had to be defined by the central government. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those relations are spelled out in the constitution that was adopted three days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, and that's -- what I'm saying is constitutionally correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't affirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness is not a constitutional lawyer. He is an expert historian, but not a constitutional lawyer, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Look at page 60. Kupresanin is speaking there. Kupresanin, of course, was the head of ARK or ZOBK, depending on what period of time we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And he agrees with Karadzic. He says, "Let them appear before this assembly, which is our supreme authority. It can annul all our decisions. Let them say what they have to say. As far as I'm concerned, this assembly is in the right."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Just out of curiosity, if you look about halfway down the page -- no, skip that. I just read it earlier, apparently. Document -- Prosecution Exhibit 34 is a meeting of the Deputies Club of 28 February 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And in that meeting there is a great deal of discussion over the threat by the Krajina, the Bosnian Krajina, to secede and become a republic of its own; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And it was the day before the meeting in Banja Luka where Karadzic and other leaders attended to try to deal with that problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Page 19, Nikola Erceg is speaking. Do you know who Nikola Erceg is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe at this time or shortly thereafter he was the president of the executive council of the ARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He says the following: "As regards tomorrow, I am simply afraid of what may happen in Banja Luka. I would add that there are indications that Seselj's men, his soldiers, may come tomorrow, too, as a show of strength. The condition for their arrival is the fact that tomorrow is the first day of the referendum. So there will be dramatic events in Banja Luka tomorrow at the same time and in the same place. That's the first day of the referendum. Seselj's show of strength, the session of the Krajina Regional Assembly, with a de facto undefined agenda, in my view, in the sense that it is one thing to define the agenda but the expectations or, rather, there will probably be a proposal to include adoption of the decision on the proclamation of the Republic of Krajina." So at least in Erceg's view, that next day was to be a very crucial day as to whether or not the Krajina would go off on its own; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. I'm nearly finished, Dr. Donia. One or two more questions. I want to refer to the conclusions that you shared with the Trial Chamber at the close of your direct testimony, what seems like two or three weeks ago. One of the things that you said to the Chamber was that you -- by going through all these documents, you were struck by the fact that there was very little mention of non-Serbs in the various Serb deliberative bodies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I assume that you have spent some time reading transcripts of proceedings of Muslim deliberative bodies, SDA meetings, SDA Municipal Assemblies, HDZ meetings, HDZ assemblies -- HDZ assemblies, all of those other deliberative bodies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some. Much less than -- than I have with these.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Have you made any kind of a statistical analysis regarding the frequency with which non-Muslim peoples are mentioned in Muslim deliberative bodies and non-Croat persons are mentioned in Croat deliberative bodies as compared with your observations regarding these Serb deliberative bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Look, if you will, at Prosecution's Exhibit 13 and go to page 58. First, before you go to page 58, look at the first page. What this is, is a meeting of the SDS on 12 July 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: On page 58, a speaker by the name of Abdulah Konicija was introduced to the assembly and spoke. Do you know that person's nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would conclude, based on his name and also his position, that he was a Bosnian Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The next page, a person named Rabija Subic addressed the assembly. Do you know his nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's identified elsewhere as Muslim, Bosnian Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: On the next page, Rasim Kadic addressed the assembly. Do you know what his nationality was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what he declared his nationality as.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He indicates, does he not, in the first large paragraph, that he attended the founding assembly of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The next speaker was Zlatko Lagumdzija, the Vice-President of the SDP. Do you know his nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what he defines his nationality as.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How about the next speaker, Salko Alicehajic, BH party of Yugoslavs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, I'm not sure how -- what his declared nationality is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How about Muhamed Cengic? It's pretty clear who he is; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he's definitely a Bosnian Muslim, now Bosniak, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. So it appears that not only were non-Serbs mentioned but actually were in attendance at this meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This was a practice for all three national parties, right up until the fall of 1991, to invite and receive greetings from members of other political parties at their founding assemblies and at their major convocations. So the SDA had speakers from the SDS and the SDP come to their meetings. The same with the HDZ. It was a courtesy that was a part of political party practice at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. I have no further questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Ms. Fauveau for General Talic, would you like to start your cross-examination now, at least with the introductory part?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Dr. Donia, you are now going to be cross-examined by Defence counsel for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have a few questions regarding the Second World War before I come to the year 1992. Would you be in agreement that the Serb people in the military Krajina in Croatia and the Serbian people in Bosanska Krajina shared the same destiny during the Second World War?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that Mr. Tudjman became president of Croatia in 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You know that Mr. Tudjman is a historian, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the thesis of Mr. Tudjman according to which there was no genocide against the Jewish people during the Second World War?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He advanced that thesis at one time and later retracted it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that during the Second World War, Bosnia was part of the independent state of Croatia governed by a Ustasha regime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The day before yesterday, you mentioned the Drina River. Was this river the eastern boundary of this independent state of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, whether the Drina River appeared in the speeches of Mr. Tudjman in the years 1990 and 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Frequently, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether in the 1990s the official Croatian policy was that Bosnia belonged to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that the Croatian and the Serbian peoples were constituent peoples of the Republic of Croatia during the socialist era?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that you are not a specialist in constitutional law, but do you know that Croatia proclaimed a new constitution after the elections in 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you perhaps know what the status of the Serb people was according to this new constitution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what were the demands of the Serb people in Croatia in 1990, the initial demands they made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure that the Serb people had a uniform demand. The SDS party in Croatia sought the same status for the Serbs that they had had under the socialist constitution and subsequently came to demand separate territories.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But as you said, this was later. This was a consequence. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that there were about 600.000 Serbs in Croatia in 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you give us the source of this figure, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The -- I think the actual number is 589.000 or something, residents of Croatia who identified themselves as of Serbian nationality in the 1991 census.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So there was a population census in Croatia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that in 1991, the Croatian government no longer had control over the territories inhabited by Serbs in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that would depend on when one would speak of that. And it would certainly be true that they did not have effective control over at least some Serbian-inhabited areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In that case, the census couldn't really be complete, could it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Census was taken by -- it was a -- it was taken in all Yugoslav republics, so I don't know that that would mean it could not be complete.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So would you allow for the possibility that the authorities of the Serb Krajina in Croatia in 1991 communicated their results to the Republic of Croatia so that this one could have a complete overview of the population census, complete figures for its census?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that to be the case, but it is certainly possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you can confirm that in 1991, the Serbs in Croatia and the Croats were at war against one another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at the beginning of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know when exactly the census took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe in the first three months of the year.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you sure of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that Mr. Izetbegovic became president of Bosnia-Herzegovina after the elections of 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He became president of the seven-person presidency, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you confirmed that an SS unit was formed of Bosnian Muslims during the Second World War.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Izetbegovic participated in the Second World War as a combatant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: He did not participate, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your question was "did I know". I do not know if he did or did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your report, you refer to Mr. Izetbegovic's book "The Islamic Declaration."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when that book was written?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to his introductory comments, the book was written between approximately 1990 -- or 1966 and 1970.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that it was published again in the year 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's been republished a number of times, in 1990 and since, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that in that book Mr. Izetbegovic wrote that there could be no peace and coexistence between the Muslim people and non-Muslim political and social institutions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The book is a broad discussion of his view of Muslim societies. He discusses virtually every country on the face of the earth but never mentions Yugoslavia, never mentions Bosnia. And the purpose, apparent purpose, of his book or tract is to steer a course between conservative or traditional fundamentalist Islam and modernisation, which was at that time represented best by the Shah of Iran. And in the course of this, he constantly chooses between these very modern, western, democratic norms and more traditional Islamic understanding. He -- almost every page, he's finding a middle course between those two. In the course of this, he prescribes what he believes is the best blend or middle ground between these two and defines that in a number of separate sections of the book.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the explanation, but my question was: Did you find the quotation that I gave you a moment ago in that book? Would you like me to read the quotation once again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'd like to see the book.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You haven't read that book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have read the book. I haven't memorised it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't remember this sentence from the book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't memorised it. I don't recall that sentence from the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If a passage in a book is being put to the witness, then that passage should be put in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. She has just asked the witness whether he wants to see the -- or wants her to read the passage or wants to see the passage. The witness has asked her whether she has got the book. So we'll take it up from there and we will see what the position is. Yes, Ms. Fauveau. Are you going to show the witness the passage?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, because I have written it down in Serbo-Croatian. So I ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the Serb, Croatian, and Muslim peoples were constituent peoples of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina according to the 1974 Constitution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have another question that may involve constitutional law. Did you know whether the 1974 Yugoslav Constitution envisaged the cessation of republics -- secession of republics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So I assume that you also don't know that the Yugoslav constitution envisaged the secession of peoples, of nations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with those provisions of the SFRY constitution, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the end of your examination-in-chief, you said that numerous institutions such as Crisis Staffs, War Presidencies, and various assemblies were established, which all had as their aim the formation of a state dominated by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be better to say that the aim of the Serb people was to remain within Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a different assertion. Many Serbs wished to remain in Yugoslavia, I agree, but that's not what the statement I made was as you read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But the SDS party of Bosnia wanted the Serbs to remain within Yugoslavia or did they want to create a separate state of Serbs in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as I think I've indicated, their first position was that Bosnia-Herzegovina should remain a part of federal Yugoslavia as it then existed. Their fallback or contingent position was that there should be a Serbian state created which would supersede that Yugoslav state.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you look at Prosecution Exhibit number 13, the minutes of an SDS meeting of the 12th of July, 1991, and I think it is page 54. Would you agree that the SDS, at this meeting, defined its principal objectives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that I would characterise it that way. The meeting was held on the first anniversary of the founding of the party and, of course, as a wide-ranging debate. But I don't know that it had as its objective to actually form or reform the party platform.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that on page 53 of these minutes, we note --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Mr. President, may I ask permission to read this passage in English as I don't have a French translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] The basic goal of the party is full and unconditional civil, ethnic, cultural, religious, and economic equality for Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina. There can be no leading nations, no satellite nations, no first- and second-class citizens, no state-forming and nonstate-forming elements. It is a goal of the party to improve interethnic relations, strike a balance and to establish reprocity, strengthen the civil peace. It is a goal of the party to have a federative Yugoslavia with an equal and whole federal Bosnia and Herzegovina within it." [Interpretation] Would you agree that this is after all a definition of "objectives"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a statement of goals by the president of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the HDZ and SDA issued declarations of sovereignty on the 15th of October, 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delegates of those parties passed in the assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina the declaration of sovereignty on that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the Serbs did not participate in the adoption of that declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you agree also that the Serbs were a constituent people of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was the Council of National Equality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Wouldn't that be the organ that would be competent for a declaration of sovereignty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a question of law, and I can't really answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Correct. Please do avoid putting questions that we have already an indication the witness cannot answer or should not even be expected to answer. I would suggest that we stop here; or if you have a few further questions before we go into break, you put them now. Otherwise, we break for 20 minutes or 25 minutes now and resume at 10 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another two or three questions in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... And then we'll break then.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that even after this decision taken clearly against the will of the Serb people and the interests of the Serb people, that the SDS continued to seek for a political settlement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Part of your question is a premise that it was taken against the will and interest of the Serb people, and I would not necessarily share that formulation of your assumption. I would agree that the SDS continued to participate in - both within Bosnia-Herzegovina and internationally - a quest for a negotiated solution.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we could stop now, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just before we rise, it would assist simply to know whether to get Mr. Inayat ready, whether Madam Fauveau thinks she will finish by the next break or shortly afterwards. Because if she will, we can deal with the movie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Fauveau, how much longer do you anticipate your cross-examination will last?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I will complete it before the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will resume any time between 10 to 11.00 and 11.00. I would assume that we will take the entire hour and a half following that, and then we'll obviously have a short break, and you have a full hour in which to get ready. Would that be enough?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I know Mr. Cayley intends to ask some questions in re-examination, but I think even with that, we can call Mr. Inayat and then start anew on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. Thank you, Ms. Fauveau. We'll resume at 10 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Please be seated. Could you bring in Dr. Donia, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me just a moment, Your Honour. While we're waiting, may I ask if the movie which Ms. Korner is going to play has been previously provided to us? Has it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it has. It's actually an edited version because the original runs for something like an hour plus, and we've tried to cut it down. There were two videos. I can't remember the disclosure numbers. One is of the whole area and the second is of Manjaca camp, but the two have been -- I think the technical term is "spliced together" to make a 25-minute movie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Ms. Fauveau, you can proceed with your cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, a minute ago you told me that you didn't share the opinion that the decision of the SDA and -- of deputies from the SDA and the HDZ concerning the declaration of sovereignty had been taken against the will of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I said I didn't share that formulation of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You agreed, however, that this declaration had been taken against the will of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many Serbs there were in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Could you give us a percentage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the percentage, but 37, 38 per cent. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what the percentage of votes the SDS obtained, what percentage the SDS obtained in the votes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not off -- not offhand. They received something around or slightly over 80 per cent of the votes of Serbs living in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So the vast majority of the Serbian population was following the policies of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The vast majority of the Serb population voted for the SDS in November 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were being examined, your conclusions were that in the records of various Serbian organs you had seen a reference to a guarantee to the rights that were guaranteed for other people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. A number of statements which either instruct subordinate organs or on the face of them speak to the very broad issue of guaranteeing the rights of either Muslims and Croats or other peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you say whether these were particular forms of guarantees or whether it was the will of the SDS to provide the three peoples with exactly the same rights?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the Prosecutor's document Exhibit number 17. I think it is under tab 14. These are notes of the assembly of the Serbian people of the 21st of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that on page 11 Momcilo Krajisnik declared the following, this is the first paragraph: [In English] "In everything we do, we should consider our complex social and political situation. All the proposed solutions must be based on the Constitution and the laws, reflecting the interest of the Serbian people, but not at the expense of other peoples in Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And paragraph 3, he said the following: [In English] "The basic principle we should observe in our activities is not to impose the will of the Serbian people on other peoples. We should respect the legitimate will of the Muslims and Croats..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you going to finish that sentence or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, you're in French.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you do it or would you like me to do it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So Momcilo Krajisnik said: [In English] "We should respect the legitimate will of the Muslims and Croats, but we must not underestimate our advantages expressed through the realistic ratio of political forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina. We must not cede our rights to others."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And at the end of the following paragraph he stated: [In English] "Therefore, we are in favour of a life of equal peoples, a parliamentary life, free of the abuse of the majority vote and the imposition of one people's on others. The essence of our effort is clear: A life together Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in our shared state. The assembly, gentlemen, is Serbian, but it also belongs to all those who want a common homeland."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were being examined, you said that the SDS created the Serbian Municipal Council -- National Council?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Serbian National Council in October 1990?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the importance of this organ was the fact that it had to show that the SDS did not want to accept the results of the electoral process since it insisted on creating institutions which would guarantee the right of veto - the absolute right of veto - to the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A veto, yes. I'm sorry, I missed part of the translation. I have it now. Yes, I used words similar to that anyway. This was the organ that all three national parties had hoped would be created as one of the three chambers of the assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it was not. Instead, this council of nationalities was provided for within the two existing chambers of peoples and municipalities, and I think I mentioned that the SDS was the only party among the three national parties that formed a body on its own which asserted these rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But this institution which should have been created and in the end was not was the Peoples' Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it should have been created. It was a chamber of peoples that was debated and rejected by the assembly in February of 1990 when it was considering the - either February or July 1990 - when it was considering bodies to establish.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this chamber of peoples would have guaranteed to the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina the right to a veto?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Limited right to review and veto certain legislation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, naturally. But this right to a veto would have been guaranteed in the same way to the Serbian people, to the Croatian people, and to the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in a programme, in its electoral programme, the SDA also promised the creation of a chamber of peoples?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe the HDZ did also. All three of them made a major point in the electoral campaign of advocating the creation of a chamber of peoples, complained about the failure to organise it earlier, and promised to organise it after the elections had been held.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now going to go to the subject of regionalisation. You said regionalisation was a term used by the SDS in order to establish zones which would be under the control of one nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One nationality and a single party.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina, before the election in 1990, did it have a regional territorial organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't understand. Perhaps the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter corrects himself. A regional territorial election.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was only one election, and that was on November 18, 1990. And then there was two weeks later a follow-up runoff. But there were no regional elections from that time forward, to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau, if you are referring to any event in particular, you are in cross-examination and you have every right to put a direct question to him. So you can lead the witness in that sense. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Before the elections in 1992, did the municipality -- was the municipality united into certain associations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were several associations of municipalities in existence prior to the elections. Most significant was the city of Sarajevo which was -- consisted of ten municipalities. And I also mentioned the Bihac association of municipalities, and the Banja Luka association of municipalities. Those all existed prior to the election.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you agree that the association of municipalities of Banja Luka existed before the elections in 1992 -- 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether before the elections in 1990 the municipality of Kljuc was part of the association of municipalities of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not offhand. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you have a look at Prosecutor's Exhibit Number 3. It's the first document in the first binder. When you were being examined, you said that this document reflected the decision of the municipal assembly of Kljuc of the 10th of April 1991, the decision to join the association of municipalities of Bosanska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you read the first paragraph after the title "The Decision" or, if you prefer, I could read it myself. It's a document in Serbo-Croat so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] Decision: We hereby confirm the previously-taken decision on the Kljuc municipality joining the association of municipalities of Banja Luka, and we hereby establish that the Kljuc municipality is part of the regional association of Bosanska Krajina, that is now the autonomous region of Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, wouldn't it be right to say that this decision confirms the status quo, that is to say, the existence of the municipalities Kljuc in the association of the municipalities of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. First of all, this document refers to an act of 10 April 1991. It clearly dates from a later time. It dates after the ZOBK had taken the name ARK, and it asserts the continuity of the old -- let me call it the old association of municipalities of Banja Luka and the SAO Bosanska Krajina. I would not, however, take that to be an affirmation of that continuity. It is the view of that assembly that that continuity existed. Other municipalities revoked their membership in the Banja Luka association of municipalities at the same time that they voted to join the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the decision of the 10th of April, 1991, wasn't it a decision confirming the status quo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You read the first sentence of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as I say, that -- we haven't read the first sentence of the document, I don't believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps, Dr. Donia, we could do as we have done on the previous location when you read the totality of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, I looked now. I believe we have read it before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. And we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- in totality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You preferred at the time to read it yourself and have it translated to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So perhaps you -- now that you are being referred to the very first paragraph, I know that you have read it, I do not have the capacity to memorise it, but perhaps you could read it again and so that we will have the benefit of a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was read by someone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. But anyway -- yes, exactly. Perhaps we could have it read, and then at least we will have the benefit of knowing what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll be glad to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc, at a session dated 10 April 1991, confirmed its existence and further adherence to the association of municipalities of Banja Luka and - I can't read this - selected, elected its representatives to the assembly of -- of the municipalities, it therefore has ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you agree that the municipality of Kljuc, on the 10th of April, 1991, confirmed its existence and the fact that it would remain within the Municipal Assembly within the association of municipalities of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if I can just be clear about this. This document dates from a later time and refers to the decision of the 10th of April, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. Would you have a look at the Prosecution's Exhibit P4. It is the following document, I think. It's a decision of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc, of Titov Drvar, in which this municipality joins the association of municipalities of Bosanska Krajina. This is April 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that this decision reflected a decision of the SDS which was taken in April.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at page 2 of this document, of the decision of Titov Drvar. In paragraph 2 -- doesn't paragraph 2 state: [Previous translation continues]... [In English] "... question at the session held on 29 March 1991, the Executive Committee finalised the draft decision to conclude an agreement joining Titov Drvar municipality to the community of municipalities of Bosanska Krajina"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So had this decision already been taken in March 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I indicated in my direct testimony, the SDS decision to initiate this process can be dated to early January 1991 according to the party's announcement in April of 1991, and in fact, this document, in the prior paragraph from that that you read, indicates that discussions occurred subsequent to the 25 January 1991 meeting. So the deliberations or discussion about doing this dated to early January. The decision of the SDS board, as announced publicly somewhat later, was taken, I think, on the 6th of April, 1991, at which point, within a few days, it became reality in the Serb-majority municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity of seeing this SDS decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, could you tell us what the percentage of Serbs in the municipality of Titov Drvar was in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's very high. I can take a look. According to page 48 of my report citing the 1991 census, it was 16.608 persons or 97 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the percentage was in 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that today this town is called Croatian Drvar, Hrvatski Drvar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in December 1991, January 1992, several municipalities that did not have a Serbian majority joined the ARK.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us about the decision concerning the territory, the entire territory of these municipalities. Did this decision concern the entire territories or only part of this territory?
