This, Your Honours, is the village of Prhovo, which is about 11 kilometres north-east of Kljuc town, a village that was attacked on 1st of June, Your Honours. Amongst the victims were many elderly women. Many who were killed, their bodies have been exhumed. And soon we will see a cemetery where their remains have been buried. This white square that you see at the bottom of your screens is a new cemetery on the road from Kljuc heading towards Grabovica. This is Grabovica, located south of Kotor Varos. This is the Grabovica school. And I think it's best for witnesses to point out what happened here. Overwhelmingly Serb village located in a valley. This is the back side of the school. This, Your Honours, is the settlement of Vrbanjci, also located about 15 kilometres south of Kotor Varos. So this is a destroyed mosque that you see in the centre of your screens with the dome. This is the upper half of Vrbanjci, and, Your Honours, this is the lower half of Vrbanjci, which is separated by a small river. We are flying over Vrbanjci, Your Honours, and now looking east in the direction of Dabovci. And Hanifici village is further 3 kilometres to the east of Dabovci. Unfortunately, it wasn't a clear day when this footage was made. This, Your Honours, is Dabovci, the main Kotor Varos-Teslic road running in front of it, attacked mid-August 1992. The road that you see in the background is the road leading towards the village of Hanifici from Dabovci, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are listed in paragraph 38 at page 15, starting with the third killing listed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This, Your Honours, is the village of Hanifici, approximately a hundred houses, all destroyed during the attack on the 13th of June, 1992. There, Your Honours, are the settlements of Hanifici and Cerkin Brdo that is north of Hanifici and that's the direction where Hanifici and Cerkin Brdo are. And we might get a distant view of those two settlements. This is still Hanifici. This, Your Honours, is a distant view of Hanifici and Cerkin Brdo, also attacked mid-August 1992. Your Honours, now we'll be heading towards the Kotor Varos town. This is Kotor Varos town, Your Honours, located south-east of Banja Luka. Quite a few settlements in the town known as Cepak, Kotor Varos, Kotoriste, Ravni in the distance in the mountains. This is the main road, Your Honours, where the main buildings are located, police station, Municipal Assembly building. And this is the sawmill where female detainees are brought from Muslim and Croat villages. This, Your Honours, is a sawmill. We'll see soon a Catholic church in the distance. Here, centre of your screens. Destroyed. This is the football ground, Your Honours, and to the right of the football ground is the Prijedor medical centre, Prijedor hospital, a scene of a massacre which witnesses will talk about. I believe we have come to the end of the aerial footage, except that when witnesses talk of a grassy plot in front of the hospital, that's the last scene we'll see here. I'm refocusing on the grassy plot, this, Your Honours, in front of the hospital. And a few -- I think after this is the Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, if we can run the rest of the video through.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, we've only got ten minutes. I think we need to keep the comments short.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. Could we play the rest of the video.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: This is a dirt road, Your Honours, leading to the military farms, and this is the Manjaca military establishment. It's about 3 kilometres from the establishment where the main gate is. Main gate to your left. Main gate. This is where we have just come from, and this is the parking area in front of the main gate. Administration building 10 metres from the main gate on the right-hand side. This is to the left of the main gate, very close. Observation tower about 200 metres from the main road, facing the main gate. Some of the barracks, the cattle sheds. In all, I think there are about 13 or 14. And this is shed number 1. This is inside of the shed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is this where prisoners were kept, Mr. Inayat?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. The shed just in front of us is the place that was used as a kitchen, and to the left, so the backhand side of the shed number 1. I think we can fast forward this because basically this is taking a view of some of the other sheds. So if we can fast forward here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we could fast forward.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. That's it. And this is once again the administration building, and the only thing we wanted to show you was the office of the camp Commander, Colonel Bozidar Popovic. This, Your Honours, is an Orthodox church which was being built in 1992, located about 3 to 4 kilometres from the detention camp. Prisoners were brought here for allegedly forced labour. I think this brings us to the end of the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Your Honours, that was merely so that one can get a picture of the area. Of course, it can always be replayed once you've heard the evidence when it perhaps may mean more. May I ask that become Prosecutor's Exhibit 447.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Your Honours, on Monday, may I explain that I will not be here because I'm professionally obliged to be in the Court of Appeal in England on Monday, but Mr. Cayley and another member of the team, Mr. Koumjian, will be here on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate you informed the Trial Chamber

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that. I thank you, Ms. Korner, for informing the Trial Chamber of your absence on Monday coming. We have got very few minutes. What do you propose to do on Monday? Which witness, by number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I've forgotten what his number is now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it according to the schedule that you had given to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That list -- that order will be followed. I'm reminded it's 7.99, the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that is one witness, Mr. Ackerman, in regard to whom you had asked for a delay. Do you maintain your position or do you withdraw that position now? Because otherwise we will have to decide it here and now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm working through the material. It took me a long time to finish Donia. I started on it last night. They have supplied us with all the of the translations that I think were missing, and I am reasonably satisfied that we could proceed normally, that there will be no problem, and if one develops -- I'll be working all weekend. If one develops on Monday, I'll just have to tell you on Monday, but I don't think there will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. One last thing. How long do you anticipate this witness to be engaged in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that was what we were discussing just before Your Honours came in. We're not sitting next Friday. I have forgotten why not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are not sitting next Friday because I need to be away, and we are not sitting on Monday and Tuesday because Mr. Ackerman has to be away. And we will be announcing -- and also that I had told you that Judge Janu is required to be in Prague in February, and that is going to be on the 7th. So basically we will not be sitting on the 7th as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So that's -- so we'll only be sitting Monday. Monday to Wednesday of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In that case, I have no doubt at all that the witness will take the whole week. And I don't -- he may not finish if it's only three days. We -- Mr. Koumjian, who will be calling him, estimates that examination-in-chief won't finish until the Tuesday morning. We'll just have to -- I don't think he's going to be very happy. He's been here since Tuesday, regrettably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The weather has been good.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sort of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we will reconvene on Monday morning at 9.00 sharp. I thank you. I also thank the interpreters for their cooperation. As usual, you have been extremely cooperative, and that's it. The Court will rise now, and we will resume on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 4th day of February, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.52 p.m.,
